title: January 6 Voices, Testimony & First-Person Record
methodology: Each J6-V record identifies the speaker category, source setting and evidentiary character of an account. First-person testimony is preserved as testimony and is not automatically treated as independently established fact.

records.title: Officer accounts of conditions at the Capitol
records.summary: First-person accounts from officers can document what an individual officer saw, heard, experienced and did during the response.
records.limitation: An officer's direct observation can establish that officer's experience; it does not by itself establish what every officer, commander or agency knew or experienced.

records.speaker_group: Members of Congress and congressional staff
records.title: Accounts from inside the congressional proceeding
records.summary: Members and staff described the electoral-count proceeding, evacuation, sheltering, communications and continuation of the joint session.
records.limitation: Personal recollection should be distinguished from the official Congressional Record and independently timestamped events.

records.source_type: TRANSCRIBED INTERVIEW / PUBLIC STATEMENT / DOCUMENTED COMMUNICATION
records.title: Accounts concerning constitutional duties and executive-branch decisions
records.summary: Statements and testimony from executive-branch personnel can illuminate discussions, decisions and perceived responsibilities before and during January 6.
records.limitation: A witness can reliably describe a conversation they participated in while still offering interpretation or recollection that requires comparison with documents and other witnesses.

records.title: State and local election officials described certification pressures and disputes
records.summary: Election officials provided accounts concerning administration, certification, recounts, communications and challenges following the 2020 election.
records.limitation: A witness account about pressure, communications or election administration should be separated from the legal resolution of any particular election claim.

records.title: Accounts of authorization, mobilization and deployment
records.summary: Military and Guard witnesses described command relationships, requests, authorization, mission preparation and deployment associated with the Capitol response.
records.limitation: A participant's recollection of one stage should not collapse request, authorization, mobilization and physical deployment into a single event.

records.speaker_group: Demonstrators and people who entered the Capitol
records.title: Participant accounts require conduct-specific context
records.summary: Statements from demonstrators and people who entered the Capitol can document motives, perceptions and conduct when preserved alongside video, communications and applicable case records.
records.limitation: One participant's stated motive does not establish the motive or conduct of other participants; legal status must be described case by case.

records.title: Contemporaneous observers preserved events in real time
records.summary: Journalists and visual documentarians created photographs, video, audio and contemporaneous accounts that can help establish location, sequence and observable conduct.
records.limitation: A recording can strongly establish what appears within its frame or audio, but interpretation outside that captured context may require additional evidence.

records.title: Disagreement and changed recollections remain visible
records.summary: When material accounts conflict or a witness later clarifies, corrects or changes an account, the record should preserve the relevant versions and compare them with independent evidence.
records.limitation: Preserving conflicting accounts does not require giving equally supported and unsupported claims equal evidentiary weight.
